INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE JULY 12, 2021
  OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT MEETING

The Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District meeting will be closed to the public in
compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-
19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting will be conducted via teleconference with members
participating remotely. Considering this, the customary meeting format has been modified.
Even with this change in format, the City is still encouraging public participation and wishes to
make residents aware of the following opportunities for participation:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. They
  will be shared with the District Board Members prior to the meeting and will be made
  part of the permanent record. We ask that you provide those emails before 7:00 p.m.
  the day before the meeting. Please be advised that public comments submitted by
  emails or any other format to the City are public records that will be made
  available for public viewing.

  3) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may
  email planning@cityoflaverne.org by 7:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting with a phone
  number and the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate
  time during the meeting for your comment.

  4) Additionally, if you wish to participate via Zoom, you will need to register before 8:00
  a.m. on the date of the meeting and please be aware that space is limited.

  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_knXkZigjRj2aNo3avUr-Lg

  You will be provided a link after registering and will have the ability to watch the
  meeting live. If you wish to speak during the meeting, you can “raise your hand” as
  appropriate on the current agenda item(s). Once it is your turn to speak, you will be
  brought into the meeting and have the ability to speak and turn on your video when
  called upon.

   OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, June 7, 2021

1.  The teleconference meeting was called to order by Chairperson Craig Walters at 8:30a.m.
  Mr. Walters stated that questions can be emailed to planning@cityoflaverne.org.

  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Jason Miller, Matt Forgey, Micky
  Rehm, and Marianne Stark (late). City Representative present: Community Development
  Director Eric Scherer. Others present: Leah Skinner.

  Mr. Scherer congratulated Chairperson Walters for serving on the Board for 25 years.

2.  CALENDAR

  City Council Public Protest Hearing – Monday, June 7, 2021 @ 6:30p.m.
  Mr. Scherer stated that he and Chairperson will be presenting to City Council tonight.
  Mr. Scherer stated that reappointments are due for Chairperson Walters, Ms. Rehm, Ms.
  Stark.

  Cool Cruise – Saturday, September 11, 2021

  Cruisin La Verne – Saturday, November 20, 2021

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES May 3, 2021

  It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Ms. Rehm to approve the minutes as
  submitted. Motion carried by a 4-0 vote.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Election of Officers for Remainder of the Year - Vice-Chair, Secretary,
  Treasurer – It was moved by Chairperson Walters and seconded by Mr. Miller to
  elect Ms. Rehm as Vice-Chairperson, Ms. Stark as Treasurer, and Mr. Forgey as
  Secretary. Motion carried by a 4-0 vote.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the elections must take place during the first meeting of
  the calendar year.

  B.  Annual Report of the District – Mr. Scherer attached a copy of the report that will
  be presented at the City Council meeting.

  C.  Proposal for Craft Fair – Carmel Plotkin presented a proposal for an Artisan Fair
  for local artisans. Board members asked questions regarding the vendor criteria

  1
   and location. The Board expressed support for the event. Ms. Plotkin will prepare
  more information and present a potential date in the future.

  D.  Cool Cruise Update – Mr. Scherer stated that he has not received any updates
  from Craig Hoelzel.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  D Street Closure – Update and Comments Received – Mr. Scherer attached
  emails received from two Old Town business owners. Both expressed concerns
  with the continued street closure scheduled in the beginning of August.

  The board discussed the timing for re-opening “D” Street. Mr. Scherer suggested
  aligning the re-opening with the Gold Line’s closure at the “D” Street railroad
  crossing.

  The board agreed that it’s best to keep the street closure in place until mid to late
  August. Mr. Forgey asked if it’s possible to explore a permanent street closure.
  Mr. Scherer stated that Public Works would not support a closure due to traffic
  circulation but it can be placed on the agenda and discussed with Council if the
  Board wished to advance the concept.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A.  City Report (Eric Scherer): Modified 4th of July parade and fireworks show. The
  parade will take place on Saturday, July 3rd in respect for the churches.
  B.  University Report (Jason Miller): More information will be provided after June
  15th but he anticipates a greater number of students on campus and in the
  classrooms.
  C.  Marketing (Micky Rehm): Ms. Rehm asked if the Beer and Wine Walk will be
  added to the calendar. Mr. Scherer stated that more guidance is needed from the
  County and OSHA.
  D.  Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): None
  E.  Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None
  F.  Financial Report: None

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  No public comments were received.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:22 a.m., to the next meeting to be held on Monday, July 12,
  2021 at 8:30 a.m.

  Respectively submitted,
  2
 _____________________
Natalie M. Hiatt

   ATTACHMENT A

  ANNUAL REPORT OF THE OLD TOWN LA VERNE
  BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT FOR THE 2021-2022 FISCAL YEAR

  FINANCE

During the 2020-2021 fiscal year the Old Town La Verne Business Improvement
District (“District”) received approximately $14,000 from the District fees paid by the
businesses within the District. While the budget was prepared at the beginning of
COCID, the events were budgeted as normal, but virtually no events occurred during
the year. The reduction of revenue in 2020/2021 from not having these events
resulted in the use of approximately $6,000 of the $126,000 in reserves. The
proposed 2021-2022 annual budget provides for approximately $40,000 in ongoing
annual expenditures and $42,000 in capital projects, with projected revenues of
$46,500. These Capital Improvement projects (Mainiero Square and Tree Lights)
where postponed in the last fiscal year due to COVID. These figures are assuming
that only a modified (reduced) Wine Walk could occur in the spring. It is now
expected that later this year a budget amendment request will be made to include
more events which will increase the expenditures but also the revenues the District
will receive.

  PROMOTIONS

Unfortunately, due to the COVID pandemic, almost no events were allowed to occur.
While the District was hopeful that in the fall of 2020 events might have been able to
occur, these were all cancelled as a result of State and County orders, restricting
mass gatherings. In the summer of 2020, D Street was closed to vehicles to allow for
restaurant expansion into the street. Many of these restaurants have shared that
without this change, many of them wouldn’t have survived the pandemic. At this time,
it is expected that the closure will remain in place until the University begins their fall
semester in August 2021.

The positive news is at this time it appears that the restrictions will be lifted as soon
as June 15, 2021, allowing for the planning of events, potentially modified slightly, to
occur as they would in a normal year. The 2020 Cool Cruise event has been
postponed multiple times, but now looks to be locked-in for the current announced
date of Saturday, September 11, 2021. It is also likely that a Beer Walk event in the
fall, Halloween event in October, Cruisin La Verne Car Show in November, and the
Holiday Stroll in December will all occur.

Support for all of these events includes logistics, advertising and other publicity,
which in turn brings the public and new businesses to Old Town. The continued
business growth in Old Town is a result of these efforts. The Old Town La Verne
Business Improvement Association has taken on more of the responsibilities of
marketing the Old Town businesses and events. They continue to use social media
and their website, www.oldtownlaverne.org, to help promote the area.
   ANNUAL BREAKFAST MEETING

The Annual Meeting of the OTLVBID was held virtually on March 1, 2021. The
District Board heard an update on the Gold (“L”) Line project and the Mayor’s State of
the City address.

  ONGOING SERVICE/MAINTENANCE

The District provides ongoing service for Old Town businesses by way of regular
sidewalk cleaning, landscape maintenance and replacement, and through funding of
the electrical costs for the lights in Old Town street trees.

  MAJOR PROJECTS

This year it was expected that Phase 2 of the tree lights would occur, which would
have included the expansion of electrical and irrigation primarily on Bonita Avenue in
order to plant new trees and expand the tree lights in the future. The other major
project that was expected to occur was the Mainiero Square re-design. Both of these
projects were placed on hold as a result of COVID. Both are, however, scheduled to
proceed in the next fiscal year and are listed in the City’s Capital Improvement
Program.

OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT
  IVIINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, July 12,2021

I  The teleconference meeting was called to order by Chairperson Craig Walters at 8:3la.m.
  Mr.Waltersstatedthatquestionscanbeemailedto@.
  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Jason Miller, Marianne Stark, Micky
  Rehm, and Matt Forgey (arrived late). City Representative present: Mayor Tim Hepburn,
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer, and Secretary Natalie Hiatt. Others
  present: Leah Skinner, Craig Hoelzel, and Cindy Vallejo.

2.  CALENDAR

  Cool Cruise - Saturday, September ll,202l

  Cruisin La Verne - Saturday, November 20,2021- Mr. Hoelzel stated that the event is
  scheduled for the weekend before Thanksgiving instead of the weekend after and
  requested approval from the Board.

  It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Ms. Stark to confirm the Cruisin La Veme
  event for November 20,2021. Motion was carried by a 5-0 vote.

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES June 7,2021

  It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Ms. Stark to approve the minutes with
  changes regarding the discussion of the D Street Closure. Motion carried by a 4-0 vote.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Beer Walk Event - Ms. Rehm stated that an event in September might be too soon
  and it may be a better idea to hold a Wine Walk in October or a combined Beer and Wine
  Walk.

  Mr. Scherer stated that he is not sure what regulations are in place for this type of event.

  Chairperson Walters stated that he prefers holding the Wine Walk in the spring and
  holding an outdoor Beer Walk in the fall.

  Ms. Stark and Mr. Forgey agreed that they should keep the Wine Walk for the spring.

  Ms. Rehm stated that it's a struggle to get breweries to participate in October due to
  Oktoberfest events.

  Mr. Scherer stated that he will make contact with County for more direction.
  I
   B.  Cool Cruise Update - Mr. Hoelzel stated that 500 cars are registered for the show
  and the band The Answer is playing. Proceeds of the event will benefit the La
  Veme K-9 Foundation. Mr. Hoelzel stated that the food vendors will include
  peanut brittle, shaved ice, and baked potato.

  Ms. Stark asked if shaved ice is too similar to Granny's Yogurt. The board
  decided that it would be okay if they were placed further away from the shop.

  Mr. Hoelzel stated that he is working with the Fire Department to get September
  I lth memorabilia to display. He asked if it woutd be appropriate to invite the
  Health Department to set-up a vaccination booth.

  Mr. Miller stated that the Health Department is looking for more outreach and
  opportunities to promote the vaccine.

  C.  University of La Veme - Freshmen Welcome Dinner - Cindy Vallejo of
  University of La Verne stated that the restaurant crawl is scheduled for Monday,
  August l6th from 5:00-7:00pm and that she is hopeful to have the band perform at
  Mainiero Square.

  Mr. Scherer reminded the Board that the band is in the budget for this year

  Ms. Rehm requested that the event be changed from a Monday due to several
  businesses being closed that day.

  Ms. Vallejo stated that she would look into another date and email the group with
  more information.

  Ms. Rehm suggested that she email everyone because the retail businesses may be
  interested in offering special discounts to the students.

  Mr. Scherer requested sending the email from the City on behalf of Ms. Vallejo.

  D.  Future Board Meeting Logistics - Mr. Scherer discussed in-person meetings
  versus virrual and hybrid options.

  The Board agreed upon an in-person meeting going forward. Ms. Stark suggested
  an outdoor meeting on Chase's patio and Ms. Rehm suggested Roberta's or her
  shop as a back-up.

  Mr. Scherer stated that he would research holding the meeting on Chase's patio.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  D Street Closure - Chairperson Walters stated that at the last meeting they
  extended the closure no longer than the opening of the University. The situation

  2
   has since changed and on June 28th the Association met and discussed reopening
  sooner,

  Mr. Scherer stated that he has added this item to go before the City Council on
  July l9th. In anticipation to the Board and Council's vote the businesses will be
  notified of the reopening. Mr. Scherer expects that the Public Works Department
  can have the street open as early as Thursday, July 22"d. Mr. Scherer stated that
  because the closure is meant to be a final decision and due to potential negative
  community comments, we want the item to be discussed at an open meeting.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that the survival of the businesses is most important and if
  the businesses want to reopen the street he would be in support.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the merchant parking passes will resume once the
  University returns. He will notifu businesses and they can obtain their permit by
  August 2i'd.

  Ms. Rehm noted that there have been many negative comments from customers in
  the past 2-3 weeks complaining about parking and the street not being utilized.
  Ms. Rehm stated that we need to pay attention to these complaints and open as
  soon as possible.

  Mr. Scherer stated that there is still an option for interested restaurants to build
  out into parking spaces.

  Mr. Forgey stated that he would be in favor of a permanent closure but not in its
  current state.

  It was moved by Mr. Forgey and seconded by Mr. Miller to recommend the
  immediate reopening of D Street to City Council. Motion was carried by a 5-0
  vote.

  After fuither discussion of permanent closure it was decided that more
  information is needed before proceeding. The Board will continue the discussion
  at a later date.

  B.  University Report (Jason Miller): None
  C.  Marketing (Micky Rehm): Ms. Rehm asked if the Board wants to continue

  3
   The Board discussed the Holiday Stroll and Halloween event. Mr. Scherer stated

  D.  Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): Ms. Skinner stated the Chamber has partnered
